preamble: Spirantization of the voiced retroflex stop /ɖ/ to the voiced dental fricative /ð/, with simultaneous loss of retroflexion. The best-documented case is Mantauran Rukai (Taiwan), where all Proto-Rukai voiced stops spirantized: *b > v, *g > h, and both *d and the retroflex *ɖ (written dr) merged as ð (written dh). Outside Mantauran the change is not reported, so it is a rare, dialect-specific development rather than a recurrent cross-linguistic shift.

examples.note: Proto-Rukai *ɖ (dr) became ð in Mantauran, merging with the reflex of *d (cf. *da'ane > dha'ane 'house').
Budai keeps the retroflex stop ɖ where Mantauran has the dental fricative.
Word-internal *ɖ shows the same spirantized reflex.
The other Rukai dialects keep /ɖ/; only Mantauran has /ð/.
